name: Engaged Buddhism
summary: Engaged Buddhism, a term Thich Nhat Hanh coined in the 1960s, applies Buddhist practice to social and political suffering: nonviolence and the prevention of war, simple living against greed and consumerism, sharing with the poor, speaking out against injustice without joining partisan politics, and non-discrimination. It has no common programme on government or the economy.
scope: Engaged Buddhism as Thich Nhat Hanh's Order of Interbeing precepts, the Plum Village trainings and the encyclopedia accounts define it. It excludes Buddhist socialism, Buddhist nationalism and pacifism in general, which are separate subjects.

aliases.quote: The terms “engaged Buddhism” and “socially engaged Buddhism” were taken up
